info.title: Chat Systems API
info.description: Every error response carries `{"error": "<message>"}` with the HTTP status saying what kind of error it is.

post.summary:
An invite pointed at an account that already exists is a join, not a
registration: the holder of the link is signed in already, so all that is
left is the membership the invite promised.

Hands back a secret and its provisioning URI. Nothing is enforced yet: the
enrolment is not active until a code proves the authenticator actually has
it, or people lock themselves out of accounts they never finished setting up.

Built-ins first, then anything registered. An unknown command is a 404 by
design: the client falls back to sending what was typed as an ordinary
message, so a typo does not vanish into an error dialog.

requestBody.description: One or more files as multipart fields

get.summary:
The author sees their own prior versions; a workspace admin sees anyone's,
and that read is audited. Everyone else gets the "edited" marker and nothing
behind it — showing every earlier draft to every reader is a different
product from the one people think they are using.

Whether to email a mention that reached nobody. On by default: somebody who
never grants push permission is exactly who it is for, and they are not going
to go looking for a switch to turn it on.

The public half of the VAPID pair, which the browser needs before it can ask
its push service for a subscription. It is public by definition; the reason
it sits behind the session is that an instance with push switched off should
not have to answer questions about it.

post.summary:
The export is the whole workspace, so this is the case where there is nothing
to import *into* yet. The name cannot come from the archive — Slack does not
put it there, not even in the manifest — so the caller sends one, and the app
suggests it from the file name.

requestBody.description: `archive` (a Slack export zip), optional `dry_run`, and for a new workspace `workspace_name`
`name` and an image field of at most 256 KiB

delete.summary:
Whoever added it, or a workspace admin. An emoji is shared vocabulary, so
removing one is a workspace decision rather than a personal one.

post.summary:
The most sensitive operation in the product: everything anyone said in a
workspace, in one file. Owner only.

get.summary:
Anybody in the workspace can see which groups exist -- a handle they cannot
discover is a handle they will mention by accident.

patch.summary:
The handle is not editable. Messages already sent carry the group id, but the
text people read is the handle, and renaming it would silently rewrite the
history of who was asked.

post.summary:
Membership is workspace membership first: a group is a shorthand for people
who are already here, not a way to reach somebody who is not.

patch.summary:
Owner-only, and audited with both ends of the change. Shortening retention
destroys data on the next nightly pass and there is no undo, so the record of
who asked for it matters more than usual.

post.summary:
Takes the archive and queues the work. The response is the run, not the
result: an import takes minutes to hours, and the client watches the row.

requestBody.description: `archive` (a Slack export zip), optional `dry_run`, and for a new workspace `workspace_name`

response_type.description:
`ephemeral` is seen only by whoever ran it; `in_channel` is posted as a
message from the command.

ConversationKind.description:
A direct message is the two-person case of a group; both are channels of a
type nobody can browse or join, and this is the name the client knows them by.

items.description:
A saved row plus the message it points at, so the panel can render without a
second round trip per item.

is_member.description:
Whether the person asking is in it. The client highlights a mention of
their own group the way it highlights their own name, and it cannot work
that out from a handle.

hard_delete.description:
Anonymise by default. Hard-deleting one participant's messages makes
every conversation they were in unreadable for everyone else, which is a
destructive answer to a request that rarely asked for it.

username.description:
Slack-compatible overrides. A CI hook that posts as "CI" and a release
hook that posts as "Releases" are the same integration mechanism with
different faces, and callers already send these fields.

totp_code.description:
A TOTP code or a recovery code; absent on the first attempt, which is how
the client discovers a second factor is required.

PostPolicy.description:
Who may post. `everyone` is the default and what every channel that has
never been configured returns; `moderators` is an announcement channel,
where the people who can moderate are the people who can speak.

SavedMessageDetail.description:
A saved row plus the message it points at, so the panel can render without a
second round trip per item.

SearchScope.description:
A direct message is a channel too, but somebody searching "the channels" is
not asking to see their private threads next to them, so the scope picks
which channel types the hits may come from. Filtering by channel is asking
about channels, whatever the scope says.

client_message_id.description:
The sender's own id for this send, used only to make a retry idempotent.
It is not the message id — the server owns that.

oneOf.description:
Absent means unchanged, which is how a client that predates
announcement channels keeps working.

is_member.description:
Whether the person asking is in it. The client highlights a mention of
their own group the way it highlights their own name, and it cannot work
that out from a handle.
